# Every generated file, explained

The Developer Mode installer now generates **a complete documentation website, not a skeleton**. The new starter has a responsive sidebar, mobile navigation, local search with Ctrl/Cmd+K, light/dark/system appearance, clickable breadcrumbs, page actions and a sticky page table of contents.

## What the files do

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `nextguide.config.json` | Name, description, base URL, default theme and accent |
| `content/docs/index.mdx` | Documentation homepage with live blocks |
| `content/docs/getting-started.mdx` | Onboarding guide with component examples |
| `content/docs/guides/` | Writing and customization tutorials |
| `content/docs/components/` | Component gallery that actually renders tabs, cards, accordions and more |
| `content/docs/api-reference.mdx` | Starting point for an API reference |
| `content/docs/**/_meta.json` | Navigation section names and ordering |
| `src/lib/nextguide.ts` | MDX source, plugins, code highlighting, searchable page index |
| `src/lib/nextguide-mdx-components.tsx` | Editable registry of built-in NextGuide MDX components |
| `src/app/docs/layout.tsx` | Renders `DocsSiteSidebar`, `DocsSiteSearchProvider` and `DocsSiteProviders` from the same package used by the official documentation |
| `src/app/docs/[[...slug]]/page.tsx` | Builds documentation routes, headings, breadcrumbs, page actions and TOC |
| `src/styles/nextguide.css` | Tailwind 4 utilities, package-class discovery and official design tokens imported from `nextguide/site.css`; you can override theme values here |

## Components work on first install

The installer automatically registers NextGuide's actual components with the MDX engine. You can use them in new pages immediately:

<CodeWindow title="content/docs/guide.mdx" language="mdx" code={'<Callout kind="tip" title="Ready">No separate registry installation.</Callout>\n\n<CodeWindow language="bash" code="bun run dev" />'} />

The registry includes callouts, code windows and tabs, file trees, steps, link cards, buttons, cards, tabs, accordions, input fields, tables, alerts and more. Edit `nextguide-mdx-components.tsx` to add your own.

## Where the design comes from

**There is only one documentation design.** The official NextGuide website in `apps/web` and the documentation generated by `nextguide init --developer` import the **same** components from `nextguide/site`. This includes the sticky sidebar, mobile drawer, version picker, Ctrl/Cmd+K search, appearance switcher, MDX reading column, breadcrumbs, page actions, table of contents, and previous/next links.

The official light/dark color tokens are published as `nextguide/site.css`. The installer writes a Tailwind 4 stylesheet that imports those tokens and scans `nextguide/dist`, so the package's actual UI classes are compiled into the consuming application. Inter and JetBrains Mono are loaded using Next.js font helpers, just as in the official documentation.

The older `DocsStarterShell` remains exported for compatibility with existing alpha installations, but **new installations do not use it**.

## App Router and Pages Router

The installer supports both routers, JavaScript or TypeScript, with and without `src/`. For Pages Router, it generates `pages/docs/[[...slug]].tsx` and adds the required imports to `_app`. Documentation can live at `/docs` or at the site root using `--base-path /`.

## Updating an existing site

New installations receive the full site immediately. Existing users should first preview `bunx nextguide upgrade --refresh-generated --dry-run`. A confirmed refresh backs up generated layouts and styles, preserves custom MDX and navigation, and never overwrites files without the NextGuide-generated marker.

<CodeWindow title="Preview generated files" language="bash" code="bunx nextguide init --developer --dry-run" />
